html:
The Battle of Avarayr was fought on 26 May 451 on the Avarayr plain, in today's northwest Iran, between an Armenian army under Vardan Mamikonian and the army of the Sasanian Persian king Yazdegerd II.

Yazdegerd wanted Armenian nobles to return to Zoroastrianism. The Armenians rebelled and, though they lost the battle and Vardan was killed, they kept up resistance for decades. In 484 Persia granted Armenia freedom of worship in the Treaty of Nvarsak. The Armenian church made Vardan and his companions saints, and the battle became a symbol of standing for faith and nation against great odds. It is remembered every year as Vardanants Day, and it shaped how Armenians tell their history.
